title: George Brunies and Pecora's first trombone
summary: Brunies supposedly bought Pecora's horn for nine dollars and never paid; Pecora did not recognise him when he visited the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Before I forget it, how did George Bernays get his first trombone?

He bought, he was supposed to buy my trombone for nine bucks. Yeah. And every time I see him, I say, when are you going to give me my nine bucks? He says, would you believe I got that same trombone and I ain't going to give you the nine dollars? He still got you? Yeah. That's the first horn you ever? Yeah. He tells me that all the time. I says, uh, I can't curse. I don't want to curse. Yeah. I say, hey boy, I says, when are you going to give me my nine dollars? I ain't going to give you nine dollars. I ain't going to give you a horn back. I still got your horn. Yeah. I said, good. That's pretty good. I didn't care if we could charge in. I'm a pretty good friend, you know. Yeah. You know, I didn't know him when he came in town last month. Yeah. Came at the famous door, sat at the bar.
You didn't know him? You look so different?
